title.narrative: [Consortium] Strengthening Food Security and Resilience through Integrated FSL, Health, Nutrition, and Protection services in Conflict-Affected South Darfur, Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbgtCurrent Humanitarian Situationlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will be implemented in four key localities of South Darfur: Beleil, Al Salam, Mershing, and Shattaiya. These areas face an ongoing humanitarian crisis driven by conflict and displacement, leaving lt/spangtltspangtIlt/spangtltspangtDPslt/spangtltspangt and host communities highly vulnerable. The crisis has disrupted essential services, exacerbated food insecurity, and heightened protection risks, particularly for women, children, and other marginalized groups. Food insecurity has reached Crisis (IPC Phase 3) and Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels due to disrupted agriculture and market challenges, forcing many households to adopt harmful coping strategies. Inadequate healthcare, malnutrition, and exposure to violence remain significant concerns, especially for children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWslt/spangtltspangt).lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtSectorallt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtHealthltbrgtAccess to primary healthcare services in South Darfur is critically limited, with many communities unable to obtain essential maternal and child health services. Weak disease surveillance and inadequate outbreak response mechanisms exacerbate health risks, leaving vulnerable populations at heightened risk of preventable illnesses.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtNutritionltbrgtAcute malnutrition remains a significant concern, with over 52,500 children under five and PLWs affected. Malnutrition rates surpass emergency thresholds, driven by poor access to healthcare, inadequate maternal services, and food insecurity.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFood Security and Livelihoods (FSL)lt/pgtltpgtFood production has been disrupted due to a lack of quality agricultural inputs and tools, leaving over 33,080 individuals in need of urgent interventions. Female-headed households, in particular, struggle to generate sustainable income. Poor livestock health further diminishes livelihood opportunities, worsening food insecurity in the region.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtectionltbrgtWomen and children face increased risks of gender-based violence (GBV) and exploitation. Community-based mechanisms to address protection concerns and promote resilience are lacking, leaving vulnerable groups without adequate support. Access to mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services is minimal, with 933 individuals requiring urgent assistance.ltbrgtProposed Activitiesltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtHealthltbrgt Operate and support 8 Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) to provide maternal and child health services, reproductive health, and routine immunizations.ltbrgt Train 155 health workers and rehabilitate health facilities to enhance service delivery and continuity of care.ltbrgt Strengthen disease surveillance and outbreak response mechanisms to mitigate health risks in affected communities.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtNutritionltbrgt Promote Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices to combat malnutrition targeting 25,830 people.ltbrgt Treat severe and moderate acute malnutrition through CMAM programs and 8 OTPs.ltbrgt Conduct mass screenings to identify malnourished children under five and PLWs.ltbrgt Implement complementary feeding initiatives, including food demonstrations and kitchen gardening, to improve dietary diversity and nutrition outcomes.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFSLltbrgt Distribute seeds, tools, and training to 15,000 households for local crop production.ltbrgt Provide agricultural tools like donkey ploughs and carts to vulnerable households to enhance productivity.ltbrgt Train 50 Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) and provide veterinary kits to improve livestock health.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtectionltbrgt Establish 51 community-based protection networks (CBPNS) and 4 crop protection committees to promote safety and conflict resolution.ltbrgt Provide MHPSS to 933 individuals, including case management for GBV survivors.ltbrgt Distribute dignity kits, conduct GBV awareness campaigns, and construct multi-purpose community centers.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtBeneficiarieslt/bgtltbrgtThe project will directly benefit approximately 324,964 individuals, including:ltbrgt Health: 138,965 accessing primary health care services.ltbrgt Nutrition: 58,691 benefiting from nutrition services.ltbrgt FSL: 103,308 benefiting from food security and livelihoods interventions.ltbrgt Protection: 24,000 accessing protection services, including MHPSS and GBV support.ltbrgtlt/pgt
